attempts.bug_summary: When rendering data-driven templates, the configured response chunk-size limit is not passed to the template engine. The response still uses flushing behavior, but individual generated buffers may exceed the configured maximum.

Path variables are merged after the explicitly supplied model, so a path-variable key can overwrite a value supplied by the caller. The defect appears only when both sources contain the same attribute name.

The merged model is assembled with controller render attributes before URI path variables, causing path variables to override controller-provided values when both maps contain the same key. This changes the value visible to the Thymeleaf template only for colliding attribute names.

Post-processors are ordered using the pre-processor comparator instead of their dedicated comparator. The error appears only when multiple post-processors for the same template mode have ordering characteristics that differ between the two comparator implementations.

attempts.bug_summary: When a dialect configuration does not explicitly specify a prefix, the method uses the configuration's unset prefix instead of the processor dialect's default prefix. This affects processor wrapping and element/attribute matching for dialects that provide a non-null default prefix.

When throttling is enabled, models created by standalone-element processors are queued with the wrong downstream handler whenever processing is currently stopped. This causes processable replacement or inserted models to bypass the processor handler when later resumed, so their associated processors are not applied as intended.

attempts.bug_summary: When a tag processor inserts a model before a standalone element and a later model processor runs on the same tag, the body-modification check examines the after-model twice instead of checking both queued models. As a result, the model processor can execute against an already modified body rather than raising the documented TemplateProcessingException.

Under throttling, a standalone tag that only inserts a model before itself is processed immediately instead of being represented by the deferred standalone-tag processable. This causes the inserted model and the tag's downstream handling to run outside the throttle queue, changing ordering and stop/resume behavior when no after-model is present.

The insert-immediately-after path uses the processability state associated with body-model replacement instead of the state supplied for the inserted model. As a result, a processable model inserted after an element may be delegated through the wrong handler and skip processor execution.

attempts.bug_summary: Adjacent expressions within a literal substitution are treated as a direct addition without the empty-string bridge used to force string concatenation. This changes the evaluation semantics for cases such as numeric expressions, where the original output preserves string concatenation behavior.

The generated version incorrectly marks the parser as being inside a text literal whenever an expression closes while a literal substitution is active. This stale state affects subsequent text literals after the substitution, causing their delimiters to be interpreted with the wrong state and producing malformed output for inputs that combine a substitution expression with a later text literal.

Nested expression closure incorrectly restores the parser to top-level state while a literal substitution is still active. For substitutions containing nested expressions, the outer closing delimiter can then be interpreted as the start of another substitution, producing malformed transformed output.

Value location metadata is incorrectly reported using the attribute name location instead of the value's actual location. This affects both values that terminate at the end of the sequence and values followed by whitespace, while leaving parsed content unchanged.
